universities.summary: M.O.P. Vaishnav College for Women is an autonomous University of Madras affiliated college in Nungambakkam, Chennai. Its academic undergraduate and postgraduate degrees span commerce, computing, communication, food science and social sciences. Compare exact prior qualifications, selection, shift and complete fees before applying.
universities.campusLifestyle: The central Chennai campus brings academic departments, library facilities, media and computing spaces, and student activities together. Programme shifts and practical work affect the daily timetable. The current handbook has dress, identity-card and classroom mobile-phone rules; review these before choosing a programme and commute.
universities.cityProfile: The college is at 20, IV Lane, Nungambakkam High Road, Chennai 600034. Its urban setting suits students planning a city commute. Confirm shift hours and travel arrangements before acceptance; the handbook has vehicle and parking rules, and private accommodation requires a separate arrangement.
universities.practicalExposure: Department curricula include subject-specific projects, practical work, field visits and internships. The college describes media studios, food-production facilities, computing resources and business-on-campus learning. The exact requirements vary by award; obtain the current curriculum, supervision arrangements and any materials or external-visit costs.
universities.hostelOverview: The current institutional MBA disclosure records no girls’ hostel seats, and the historical institutional report states the college does not operate a hostel. Applicants needing accommodation should obtain current college guidance and assess private housing separately. A programme offer does not include a residence place or establish its cost.
universities.dietarySupport: The 2025–26 handbook describes a college food court supplying vegetarian food and permits students to bring their own vegetarian food. It also describes Beyond Breads, a health cafeteria. Confirm current opening hours, menu, prices and any allergy requirements before budgeting; these services do not establish a residence meal plan.
universities.safetyOverview: The handbook describes in-campus medical support through Apollo Shine, accessible ramps, elevators and washrooms, and campus conduct rules. Obtain current emergency contacts and the procedure for medical help at induction. Confirm travel and private-housing arrangements separately from the college’s on-campus services.
universities.studentSupport: The college describes a campus counsellor available by appointment through its Happiness Centre, mentoring and counselling resources, and library/digital research facilities. Students receive an intranet account for academic information. Confirm current access and departmental support arrangements during induction.

M.O.P. Vaishnav College for Women is an autonomous, self-financing college affiliated to the University of Madras in Nungambakkam, Chennai. Established in 1992, it offers study in commerce, business, computing, media, food science and social sciences. These undergraduate routes describe Indian women’s school-entry conditions and regular campus study.

The central Chennai campus brings academic departments, library facilities, media and computing spaces, and student activities together. Programme shifts and practical work affect the daily timetable. The current handbook has dress, identity-card and classroom mobile-phone rules; review these before choosing a programme and commute.

The college is at 20, IV Lane, Nungambakkam High Road, Chennai 600034. Its urban setting suits students planning a city commute. Confirm shift hours and travel arrangements before acceptance; the handbook has vehicle and parking rules, and private accommodation requires a separate arrangement.

Department curricula include subject-specific projects, practical work, field visits and internships. The college describes media studios, food-production facilities, computing resources and business-on-campus learning. The exact requirements vary by award; obtain the current curriculum, supervision arrangements and any materials or external-visit costs.

The current institutional MBA disclosure records no girls’ hostel seats, and the historical institutional report states the college does not operate a hostel. Applicants needing accommodation should obtain current college guidance and assess private housing separately. A programme offer does not include a residence place or establish its cost.

The 2025–26 handbook describes a college food court supplying vegetarian food and permits students to bring their own vegetarian food. It also describes Beyond Breads, a health cafeteria. Confirm current opening hours, menu, prices and any allergy requirements before budgeting; these services do not establish a residence meal plan.

The handbook describes in-campus medical support through Apollo Shine, accessible ramps, elevators and washrooms, and campus conduct rules. Obtain current emergency contacts and the procedure for medical help at induction. Confirm travel and private-housing arrangements separately from the college’s on-campus services.

The college describes a campus counsellor available by appointment through its Happiness Centre, mentoring and counselling resources, and library/digital research facilities.
